title: Entropy and spontaneity; How much? The amount of chemical change
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Chemistry (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-30-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: R2.1#c08 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; R2.1#c02 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; R2.1#c03 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; R2.1#c04 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Molar concentration
items.clue: The amount of solute per unit volume of solution.

items.label: Coefficient (stoichiometric coefficient)
items.clue: The number written in front of a formula in a balanced equation.

items.label: Mole ratio
items.clue: Compares the amounts of two species in a reaction; read from the coefficients of the balanced equation.

questions.stem: Aluminium burns in oxygen to form aluminium oxide. Which equation for this reaction is correctly balanced?
questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide is Al₂O₃ (ions Al³⁺ and O²⁻) and oxygen gas is O₂. 3O₂ supplies 6 O atoms, matching 2Al₂O₃, which contains 4 Al atoms, so 4Al. Check: 4 Al and 6 O on each side.

questions.stem: Iron is produced by reducing iron(III) oxide with carbon monoxide: Fe₂O₃(s) + 3CO(g) → 2Fe(s) + 3CO₂(g). What is the maximum mass of iron that can be produced from 40.0 g of iron(III) oxide? A_r: O 16.00; Fe 55.85
Each reaction below is carried out in the laboratory by adding the first reactant (a solid, or potassium hydroxide solution) to a dilute aqueous acid. Which equation shows correct state symbols?
questions.explanation: Magnesium oxide is added as a solid (s); the dilute acid and the magnesium chloride formed are dissolved in water (aq); the water formed is a liquid (l).

questions.stem: Sodium hydrogencarbonate decomposes on heating: 2NaHCO₃(s) → Na₂CO₃(s) + H₂O(g) + CO₂(g). What volume of carbon dioxide, measured at STP, is produced when 16.8 g of sodium hydrogencarbonate decomposes completely? A_r: H 1.01; C 12.01; O 16.00; Na 22.99. Molar volume of an ideal gas at STP = 22.7 dm³ mol⁻¹
Hydrogen burns in oxygen, and the quantities are measured at room temperature and pressure: 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l). Which statement about the quantities shown by this equation is correct?

options.text: The mass of H₂ that reacts is twice the mass of O₂ that reacts.
Every 2 mol of H₂ react with 1 mol of O₂ to form 2 mol of H₂O.
Every 2 dm³ of H₂ and 1 dm³ of O₂ react to form 2 dm³ of H₂O.
The amount of H₂O formed equals the total amount of H₂ and O₂ used.

questions.explanation: The coefficients give the ratio of amounts in mol: 2 mol H₂ : 1 mol O₂ : 2 mol H₂O. Mass is conserved (4.04 g + 32.00 g = 36.04 g), but the amounts and masses of the individual substances are not in the same ratio.

questions.stem: A 0.399 g sample of iron(III) oxide reacts with exactly 30.0 cm³ of hydrochloric acid, with neither reactant left over: Fe₂O₃(s) + 6HCl(aq) → 2FeCl₃(aq) + 3H₂O(l). What is the concentration of the hydrochloric acid? A_r: H 1.01; O 16.00; Cl 35.45; Fe 55.85
questions.explanation: n(Fe₂O₃) = 0.399 ÷ 159.70 = 2.498 × 10⁻³ mol. The ratio Fe₂O₃ : HCl is 1 : 6, so n(HCl) = 1.499 × 10⁻² mol. With V = 30.0 cm³ = 0.0300 dm³, c = 1.499 × 10⁻² ÷ 0.0300 = 0.500 mol dm⁻³.

questions.stem:
Consider the four changes W, X, Y and Z below at 298 K. Which change results in an increase in the entropy of the system?
W: 2H₂S(g) + O₂(g) → 2S(s) + 2H₂O(l)   (exothermic)
X: NH₃(g) → NH₃(aq)   (exothermic)
Y: 2C(s) + O₂(g) → 2CO(g)   (exothermic)
Z: N₂(g) + 2O₂(g) → 2NO₂(g)   (endothermic)
